private_note: Numbers unchanged: Cedar 122, Today 108, Alder 106, Birch 90, Hazel 86. Cedar has 7 but Delegates 2, 4, 7, 8 and 11 have all vowed never to back it, so it cannot reach 9. Realistically it is Alder or failure, and failure leaves us 2 thousand better off. I keep Cedar first, keep Today narrowly above Alder, and avoid committing to Alder until I see whether the top delegates move and whether anything better is on offer.
statement: Thank you all for being straight. I'm keeping Cedar first this round: it's the best plan for households like mine, and seven of us said so. But I can count. Five delegates have said they will never vote for Cedar, so it can't reach nine. Birch and Hazel can't either, and I still can't support them; an 18 to 22 thousand dollar cut breaks a mortgage and a retirement plan. I'll be honest about Alder too. For a fourth-fifth household it's slightly worse than today, not better, so for me it isn't a free compromise. If Alder is going to be the answer, it needs the top delegates (3, 6, 9 and 12) to say plainly whether they can live with it, because without one of them it fails anyway. Tell us where you stand, and I'll decide in the final round.
